 JUDGMENT
This petition is filed seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest for the death of one Smt.Rathnamma in Road Accident.

2. The averments of the petition are as follows; That on 25.07.2022 at about 06.10 P.M., one Rathanamma was standing in front of her house, while the offending lorry coming in reverse direction in negligent manner, dashed to Rathnamma.
That due to forced impact, the Rathanamma died on spot.
That the petitioner have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/-.
That she was aged 57 years and was a house wife.

A case in Cr.No.299/2022 alleging offence punishable under section 279,
304(A) of IPC is filed against the driver of the offending lorry.
Thus prays to grant compensation as sought for.

3. The respondent No.1 in the written statement took defence that the driver of lorry while taking reverse fell into pit ditch and Rathnamma, who was standing by side of compound wall without observing the lorry, caught in middle of lorry.
Thus submits that there is negligence on part of the Rathanamma and prays to dismiss the petition.
4. On basis of the Pleadings and materials, the following issues were framed.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that Rathnamma W/o Chikkamuniyappa died in the accident that occurred on 25.07.2022 at about 06.10 P.M, on kithaganur village, Bidarahalli hobli, Bangalore which was due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing No.KA-53-AA-5933 by its driver?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
5. In order to prove their case, the petitioner no.4 got examined himself as P.W.1 and has produced 16 documents on his behalf.
The respondent No.1 examined the driver as RW-1.
6. Heard the arguments from the counsel for the petitioner and the counsel for respondent and perused the materials placed before me.

7. My findings on the above points are as follows:

Copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.2 lodged by PW-1 himself submitting that their house is situated beside road, where a pit ditch is also there.
That there is a house construction beside their house, where the building materials are being dumped in the lorry.
That on 25.07.2022, a tipper lorry loaded with M'Sand came in reverse and dashed to his mother, causing her death.
The FIR is as per Ex.P.1 in Cr.No.299/2022, alleging offence punishable under section 279, 304(A) of IPC.
The MLC from Lakshmi Super speciality Hospital is marked as Ex.P.3, which is issued on 25.07.2022 at about 07.20 PM, reporting as brought dead with alleged history of RTA.
The spot panchanama and sketch are as per Ex.P.5 showing place of accident near the house with existence of the pit.
The MVA report Ex.P.6 depicts the damages to the rear right wheel mudguard and tail lamp assemble and reported that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects.
Inquest report and PM report are as per Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.8, where opinion as to cause of death is given as due to "heamorrhage shock and crush injury to chest".

A notice to owner of lorry is given as per Ex.P.10 as required under section 133 of IMV Act,
for which a reply is given as per Ex.P.10 that one Sunil.K.N was driving the vehicle, as on the date of accident with particulars furnished of DL and insurance of driver and vehicle respectively.

Final report is as per Ex.P.9, against driver by name Sunil.K.N.
9.
Defence of respondent is that there was no negligence on part of the driver of lorry and that the said Rathnamma was careless in observing the lorry taking reverse.
Thus PW-1 was though cross examined with the above defence.
is not an eye witness to the accident and submits that he can examine any eye witness.
Thus the driver by name Sunil.K.N was summoned and examined as RW-1, where he has deposed the above noted defence.
But subjected to cross examination, admits everything questioned by counsel for petitioner.
He admits that the road was 20 feet in width and he was loading M Sand in lorry, where total weight of vehicle was 28000 Kgs, which cannot be turned in said 20 feet road.
Further admits that he could not control the vehicle and took the vehicle to the pit present over there.
That he ran away leaving the vehicle on the spot, when he heard people screaming and lastly submits that the incident happened by chance.

These admissions even did not appear as stray one.
Those admissions cannot be ruled out also.
Thus there being no malafide intention of person committing accident, same can be considered.

11. Issue No.2:
The deceased was a house wife.
Petitioners are the husband and children of the deceased.
All the 3 children of the deceased are married as admitted by PW-1.
The contention of the respondent, is that they were not dependents since all of them are married and are residing separately from each other.
Thus submits that the ration card not being produced, the joint family not proved and thus argues that they were not dependents.
In this regard PW-1 though denies that they are residing separately, submits that his father PW-1 is a retired BSNL employee and is drawing pension.
The 2nd petitioner is in London as a software engineer.
The 3rd petitioner is in Drugs control department and he the 4th petitioner is a lecturer in Government college.
Thus it is clarified that all are working and earning scrumptious money.
The deceased was a working women and house wife, the petitioners were not monetarily dependent on the deceased.
Thus the counsel for the respondent relies on authority of the Hon'ble Supreme court in " A Manavalagan Vs A.Krishnamurthy and another".

sentences.text: Reported in ILR 2004 KAR 3268 where the nature of damages on death of a person to be granted is discussed.
In the first category, the action is brought by the legal representatives, as trustees for the dependents beneficially entitled -
In the second category, the action is brought by the legal representatives, on behalf of the estate of the deceased and the compensation, when recovered, forms part of the assets of the estate.

(B) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988- SECTION 168 - POWERS OF THE TRIBUNAL UNDER - HELD - Tribunal can specify the persons to whom compensation should be paid and also specify how it should be distributed in the case of first category -
But in the case second category, no such adjustments or alteration of shares is permissible and the entire amount has to be awarded to the benefit of the estate.
(C) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - SECTIONS 168, 173 CLAIM BY THE DEFENDANTS - BASIS FOR AWARD OF COMPENSATION - HELD -
The basis for award of compensation is the loss of dependency, that is loss of what was contributed by the deceased to such claimants.
A conventional amount is awarded towards loss of expectation of life, under the head of loss to estate.
(D) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - SECTIONS 168, 173 CLAIM BY THE LEGAL REPRESENTATIVES - BASIS FOR AWARD OF COMPENSATION - HELD -
The basis for award of compensation is the loss to the estate, that is the loss of saving by the deceased.
A conventional sum for loss of expectation of life added.

Thus is is to be seen as to what is loss of estate in the instant case.

18. Liability:-
In this case, there is no disputed fact that the respondent No.1 is the insurer of the said Lorry bearing No.KA-53-AA-5933, which caused the accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: - Law contemplates two categories of damages on the death of a person -
The first is the pecuniary loss sustained by the dependent members of his family -
The second is the loss caused to the estate of the deceased-
In the first category, the action is brought by the legal representatives, as trustees for the dependents beneficially entitled -
In the second category, the action is brought by the legal representatives, on behalf of the estate of the deceased and the compensation, when recovered, forms part of the assets of the estate.

(B) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988- SECTION 168 - POWERS OF THE TRIBUNAL UNDER - HELD - Tribunal can specify the persons to whom compensation should be paid and also specify how it should be distributed in the case of first category - But in the case second category, no such adjustments or alteration of shares is permissible and the entire amount has to be awarded to the benefit of the estate.
(C) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - SECTIONS 168, 173 CLAIM BY THE DEFENDANTS - BASIS FOR AWARD OF COMPENSATION - HELD -
The basis for award of compensation is the loss of dependency, that is loss of what was contributed by the deceased to such claimants.
A conventional amount is awarded towards loss of expectation of life, under the head of loss to estate.
(D) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - SECTIONS 168, 173 CLAIM BY THE LEGAL REPRESENTATIVES - BASIS FOR AWARD OF COMPENSATION - HELD -
The basis for award of compensation is the loss to the estate, that is the loss of saving by the deceased.
A conventional sum for loss of expectation of life added.

(E) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - SECTIONS 168, 173 IF THE CLAIMANT LEGAL HEIR IS NOT A DEFENDANT WHAT WOULD BE THE POSITION -HELD - Obviously, the question of awarding any amount under the head of loss of dependency would not arise, as there was no financial dependency.

Whether the petitioners prove that Rathnamma W/o Chikkamuniyappa died in the accident that occurred on 25.07.2022 at about 06.10 P.M, on kithaganur village, Bidarahalli hobli, Bangalore which was due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing No.KA-53-AA-5933 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
So lot of admissions in such a situation comes out with fear of court, especially when there was no malafide intention of the party in committing the act, which is seen the instant case also.
These admissions even did not appear as stray one.
Those admissions cannot be ruled out also.
Thus there being no malafide intention of person committing accident, same can be considered.
However the person driving the vehicle should be at utmost care especially while reversing the heavy lorry or other heavy vehicles, where modern equipment to show any obstacles as found in new vehicle are not installed.
No precautions were taken by the driver of the lorry while taking reverse, which he admits that he lost control.
In the second category, the action is brought by the legal representatives, on behalf of the estate of the deceased and the compensation, when recovered, forms part of the assets of the estate.
(B) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988- SECTION 168 - POWERS OF THE TRIBUNAL UNDER - HELD - Tribunal can specify the persons to whom compensation should be paid and also specify how it should be distributed in the case of first category -
But in the case second category, no such adjustments or alteration of shares is permissible and the entire amount has to be awarded to the benefit of the estate.
(C) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - SECTIONS 168, 173 CLAIM BY THE DEFENDANTS - BASIS FOR AWARD OF COMPENSATION - HELD -
The basis for award of compensation is the loss of dependency, that is loss of what was contributed by the deceased to such claimants.
A conventional amount is awarded towards loss of expectation of life, under the head of loss to estate.
The basis for award of compensation is the loss to the estate, that is the loss of saving by the deceased.
Sri.Chikkamuniyappa vs M/S United India Insurance Co.Ltd on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117915687/
4 (E) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - SECTIONS 168, 173 IF THE CLAIMANT LEGAL HEIR IS NOT A DEFENDANT WHAT WOULD BE THE POSITION - HELD -
Obviously, the question of awarding any amount under the head of loss of dependency would not arise, as there was no financial dependency.
From the above authority, it can be concluded that when there is no financial dependency, the basis for award of compensation should be under loss of estate which fact is aptly applicable to the instant case.
Thus is is to be seen as to what is loss of estate in the instant case.
But the accident in the instant case occurred in 2021, where prices of every material and every work have increased to a greater extent.
It has been held in many authorities that the work of a house maid cannot be compensated in terms of money, who does every house work and takes case of her entire family being wife, mother and other relations to other person.
The respondent No.1 has failed to prove that the insurance company is not liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.
